RNA-C2-selectivity-cavity-v1.target: Mechanism linking RNA composition and phase partitioning to internal RNA-poor cavity appearance/persistence in the transcribing condensate; observable f(t) is the arithmetic mean of object-level empty-area ratios.
known_relations: B f(t) rises over 0–24 h while A remains near 0.004 after the initial measurement (initial_measurements.json).
B contains non-reference DNA reads; this does not establish the RNA composition or its time course (C01; sequence_measurements.json).
Gel-purified template length fractions have different single-preparation endpoint empty-area ratios (E02/fraction_dev.json); treatment and carryover are not matched.

Measured dense/dilute reference and variant RNA concentrations at three tie-line endpoints are available (C04/phase_measurements.json), but no phase volumes, time-resolved yields, cavity-pixel concentrations, or dynamic flux law are available.
Available tracking has positions/displacements, not persistent object-level cavity area/state histories (C03/mobility_dev.json).

hypotheses.statement: At fixed reaction chemistry, increasing the variant-to-reference RNA loading changes relative phase selectivity non-monotonically: variant enrichment in the dense phase at lower loading gives way to weaker variant partitioning at higher loading. If this creates or stabilizes variant-enriched dilute domains inside a reference-rich dense network, their area can appear as internal cavities. This phase-selectivity-to-cavity bridge is not established by the supplied endpoints.

Relative phase selectivity is constant (or the observed endpoints do not represent the B reaction); cavities arise from another amplification-associated factor such as reaction carryover or an unmeasured reaction-state change, independently of composition-driven internal domain formation.

gaps.description: Whether relative variant/reference partition selectivity changes with mixture composition beyond conservative endpoint uncertainty, and whether such a change predicts internal cavity formation rather than only bulk phase concentrations.
No matched mapping from phase concentrations/volumes or local cavity composition to the image-derived empty-area fraction; no causal separation from reaction carryover.

variables_units.Cr_dilute: reference RNA mass concentration in dilute phase, ng/uL
variables_units.Cr_dense: reference RNA mass concentration in dense phase, ng/uL
variables_units.Cv_dilute: variant RNA mass concentration in dilute phase, ng/uL
variables_units.Cv_dense: variant RNA mass concentration in dense phase, ng/uL
variables_units.K_variant: Cv_dense/Cv_dilute, dimensionless when denominator is positive
variables_units.x_v_over_r: variant/reference RNA loading ratio, dimensionless; not supplied as a measured mixture series
variables_units.f: image-derived empty-area fraction, dimensionless; supplied summary is arithmetic mean of per-object ratios

equations: K_ref = Cr_dense / Cr_dilute; K_variant = Cv_dense / Cv_dilute; alpha = K_variant / K_ref.

For a hypothetical two-phase mixture with dense-phase volume fraction phi, variant fraction in the dense phase is phi*Cv_dense / (phi*Cv_dense + (1-phi)*Cv_dilute); this is not f and cannot be evaluated without phi and matched concentrations.

A prospective testable implication of H1 is an alpha(x_v_over_r) trend that falls across unity as loading rises, followed by increased probability or area of internal cavities at fixed reaction chemistry. No functional alpha curve or f mapping is presently justified.
parameters_ranges: Use the supplied marginal concentration error ranges as rectangular bounds, not statistical confidence intervals; do not assume errors are independent or claim joint coverage.
Tie-line 0 variant partition ratio is undefined because both measured variant concentrations are zero.
No numeric range is assigned to the hypothetical cavity threshold or phase volume fraction because neither is measured.
RNA-C2-selectivity-cavity-v1.initial_boundary_conditions: Not specified for the phase endpoints. Imaging begins with similar initial empty-area fractions; no phase volume, RNA loading, or local cavity concentration initial condition is supplied.
RNA-C2-selectivity-cavity-v1.observation_mapping: The supplied f is the arithmetic mean of object-level empty-area ratios from segmented images. It is not a concentration, volume fraction, RNA mass fraction, or thermodynamic observable. Phase endpoint concentrations map only to bulk phase partition ratios under their measurement conditions.
alternatives: H0: constant relative partition selectivity or non-transferable phase endpoints; cavities instead reflect carryover or another unmeasured reaction-state factor.
Population/segmentation changes can alter summary f without same-droplet cavity formation; C03 does not supply the longitudinal state data needed to resolve this.
predictions: H1 predicts, in a controlled mixture series with fixed reaction chemistry, a reproducible decline in alpha with increasing measured variant/reference RNA loading, potentially crossing alpha=1; cavity incidence/area should change with that same loading after accounting for phase volume and imaging rules.

H0 predicts that matching carryover/reaction chemistry removes or reproduces the cavity difference independently of measured RNA mixture ratio, and that alpha need not cross unity in an assay-matched mixture series.

Current endpoint point estimates suggest alpha changes from about 37.9 (tie-line 1) to 0.335 (tie-line 2), but conservative uncertainty bounds do not establish a crossing; tie-lines are not demonstrated to be a controlled composition series.
checks: Keep concentration units consistent; each K and alpha is dimensionless.
Do not divide by a zero dilute variant concentration or report an infinite/zero partition ratio.
Check interval denominator positivity and disclose overlapping intervals.
Do not treat tie-line ordering as measured variant loading unless that relation is supplied.
Do not equate alpha or a phase concentration with image area fraction f.
Preserve preparation as the independent replication level; no field/object SEM becomes preparation-level uncertainty.
evidence_conflicts: Tie-line 1 and tie-line 2 point estimates imply opposite relative enrichment directions, but tie-line 2 conservative bounds overlap alpha=1 and experimental ordering/composition is not established.
E02 endpoint cavity differences are consistent with length-fraction dependence but are unbalanced, single-preparation, and lack carryover matching; they do not verify H1.
untested: Whether DNA read variants produce corresponding RNA species and at what abundance over time.
Whether tie-lines represent the B RNA species, comparable loading, or the imaging reaction.
Whether dilute-phase domains are internal cavities and whether they persist within individual droplets.
Whether carryover or reaction conditions explain the phenotype.
RNA-C2-selectivity-cavity-v1.dissent: The composition-selectivity-to-cavity bridge is a candidate hypothesis only. Current evidence cannot adjudicate it against carryover, population, or measurement alternatives.
RNA-C2-selectivity-cavity-v1.next_task: Have the executor compute alpha and conservative marginal-bound intervals from the supplied endpoints, test whether the ranges distinguish changing selectivity from alpha=1/constant selectivity, and return a conditional, assay-matched prediction. Keep G1 active until an explicit adjudication.

T-C2-L1-selectivity.deliverable: Executor: calculate dense/dilute partition ratios for reference and variant RNA at each tie-line; calculate alpha and conservative rectangular bounds from the supplied asymmetric marginal errors; check denominator positivity, alpha=1 overlap, and whether a composition trend is actually supported. Then state the conditional mixture-series prediction that distinguishes H1 from H0, with explicit limits on mapping to f.
T-C2-L1-selectivity.acceptance: Provide reproducible equations, values and checks; tie-line 0 variant ratio must be undefined; intervals must not be called confidence intervals; distinguish a composition trend from tie-line indexing; retain the phase-to-cavity bridge as unverified; do not claim any unexecuted result.
T-C2-L1-selectivity.reason: The missing mechanistic relation is composition-dependent relative partitioning under assay-matched conditions and its testable consequence for internal cavities; the existing endpoint values invite a quantitative comparison but are not causal proof.

reply.summary: Target: explain the emergence and persistence of the image-derived per-droplet arithmetic mean empty-area fraction f(t), not infer RNA concentration from DNA read fractions. At 0–24 h, A falls from 0.01487 to about 0.0044 while B rises from 0.01381 to 0.08918; fields/objects are not independent preparation replicates. C01 reports a 94.66% reference DNA read fraction and heterogeneous longer/shorter reads, but DNA frequencies do not determine transcribed RNA abundance. E02 shows single-preparation endpoint differences among gel-purified length fractions (M near zero, M+L 0.0445, M+S 0.0941), without matched carryover controls or RNA yield. C04 supplies phase concentration endpoints: point estimates give variant/reference partition selectivity alpha=(Cv,dense/Cv,dilute)/(Cr,dense/Cr,dilute) of about 37.9 at tie-line 1 and 0.335 at tie-line 2; zero variant concentrations make tie-line 0 undefined, and conservative intervals overlap unity at tie-line 2. These endpoints motivate but do not establish composition-dependent selectivity or its connection to image cavities. C03 confirms the available tracking lacks longitudinal same-droplet cavity state/area and track-ending reasons. Main task: compute selectivity and its uncertainty correctly, compare with the meaningful constant-selectivity alternative, and state a discriminating prediction without equating area fraction to concentration or phase volume.

requests.purpose: Quantify relative partition selectivity from observed endpoints and check whether the changing-selectivity hypothesis is distinguishable from alpha=1 or constant selectivity within supplied conservative error ranges.
requests.model_spec: For each tie_line_id, use dilute and dense records in DATA['phase_measurements.json']; concentrations in ng/uL. Compute K_ref=Cr_dense/Cr_dilute and K_variant=Cv_dense/Cv_dilute when denominators are positive, then alpha=K_variant/K_ref. Propagate provided asymmetric errors as rectangular worst-case bounds: K_lo=(Cd-dense_lower)/(Cl+dilute_upper), K_hi=(Cd+dense_upper)/(Cl-dilute_lower), and alpha bounds as K_variant_lo/K_ref_hi and K_variant_hi/K_ref_lo when positive. Report exact status if any denominator is zero/nonpositive. Compare alpha point estimates and intervals across tie-line indices, explicitly stating that index is not established as composition. Null comparator: constant alpha=1 (nonselective relative partitioning); do not fit a composition response curve from three endpoints. Output the assay-matched conditional prediction and limitations separately from arithmetic results.
